note: Short stature is documented in both the Ashkenazi Jewish cohort and the Turkish pedigree, supporting it as a recurring feature across backgrounds.

evidence.text: Phenotypes observed in Ashkenazi Jewish patients carrying the homozygous SGSM3 founder variant included hypotonia, behavioral challenges, and short stature.

source.title: Intellectual disability syndrome associated with a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 in Ashkenazi Jews
source.quote: phenotypes observed included hypotonia, behavioural challenges and short stature.

evidence.text: A homozygous stop-gain variant (p.Arg526Ter) in SGSM3 was identified in two siblings presenting with intellectual disability and short stature.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: a novel homozygous stop-gain (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) variation was detected in the SGSM3 gene in two siblings with short stature and ID findings.
